drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. We can accept the proposed $500,000 annual Base Salary and $1,000,000 Severance Amount, with severance paid in a lump sum following execution and non-revocation of the release. We have revised Cause to cover objectively defined material misconduct and uncured failure to perform after notice and an opportunity to cure. We have also deleted the non-compete and substituted tailored confidentiality and non-solicitation language. Please review the revised provisions below.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $500,000 (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to applicable withholdings. The Executive shall also be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans generally made available to similarly situated executives, subject to the terms of those plans. Any bonus or incentive compensation shall be governed by the applicable plan or a separate written agreement.

3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, the Company shall pay the Executive a severance amount of $1,000,000 (the “Severance Amount”), less applicable withholdings, in a lump sum within ten business days after the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims in favor of the Company and its affiliates. “Cause” means (a) the Executive’s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty; (b) the Executive’s willful misconduct or fraud in connection with the performance of the Executive’s duties, in either case that is materially injurious to the Company; (c) the Executive’s material breach of this Agreement or material failure to perform the Executive’s duties, which, if capable of cure, remains uncured for thirty days after written notice specifying the breach or failure and a reasonable opportunity to cure; or (d) the Executive’s misappropriation of Company funds or property. Accrued compensation and benefits through the termination date will be paid in accordance with applicable law and the governing plans.

4. CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-SOLICITATION. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential or proprietary information except as necessary to perform duties for the Company, as authorized in writing by the Company, or as required by law. This obligation does not apply to information that becomes publicly available other than through the Executive’s breach, or to disclosures protected by applicable law. For twelve months after the Executive’s employment ends, the Executive shall not knowingly solicit any employee of the Company with whom the Executive had material work-related contact during the twelve months preceding termination to leave the Company, or knowingly solicit any customer or active prospective customer with whom the Executive had material business contact during that period for the purpose of diverting business away from the Company in competition with the Company. General solicitations not specifically directed at such employees, customers, or prospective customers, and responses to unsolicited inquiries, are not prohibited. Nothing in this Section restricts activity protected by applicable law.

receiver.message_back: We accept the $500,000 Base Salary, $1,000,000 lump-sum Severance Amount, and tailored confidentiality and non-solicitation provisions, provided the release is limited to a customary release of employment-related claims and preserves accrued compensation, vested benefits, and indemnification rights. Please revise Cause so misappropriation must be material and materially injurious, and so any curable Cause event is subject to written notice and a 30-day opportunity to cure.
